profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting between the lead author of an ML survey paper and a research engineer supporting the paper release. They are preparing the final two-week push before submitting a comprehensive survey on Deep Research systems to a major ML venue and updating the companion GitHub repository. The immediate agenda is to decide how to split the remaining work for the taxonomy section, system catalog refresh, artifact packaging, and release timeline. The expected outcome is a shared plan covering who will update the survey tables, who will prepare the repository materials, what counts as the 'camera-ready package' for internal review, and when the full draft will be considered ready for circulation to coauthors.

members.name: Dr. Lina Chen
members.expertise: LLM systems, evaluation methodology, scholarly synthesis
members.background: Lina leads a university ML lab focused on AI agents and knowledge-intensive systems and is the corresponding author of the survey.
members.private_state: She wants the submission to look academically complete and stable before sending it to senior coauthors, and she is trying to avoid another disruptive round of structural edits late in the process.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the repo is updated,' that mainly means the public-facing bibliography, taxonomy diagrams, and system catalog are synchronized with the latest manuscript claims.
A 'final draft' is a coauthor-circulatable manuscript with polished prose, frozen section ordering, and all tables populated, even if minor repository cleanup remains.
The '80-plus systems' count refers only to systems that are explicitly represented in the survey's comparative catalog, not every item that might appear in auxiliary resource lists.

Asking for a 'reproducibility package' for a survey mainly means traceable source spreadsheets, citation mapping, and figure-generation scripts sufficient for internal audit rather than fully runnable external tooling.
A Friday deadline in this project context means end of day in her local campus timezone so she can review over the weekend.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: ML infrastructure, benchmark curation, documentation pipelines
members.background: Arjun maintains research repos and automation for literature-tracking projects and joined the survey effort to help scale system collection and release engineering.
members.private_state: He wants the artifact release to feel technically credible and reusable, because he expects the repository to attract outside users and possibly become a long-lived community resource.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the repo is updated,' that includes machine-readable metadata, cleaned links, schema documentation, and scripts that regenerate the public tables from the source inventory.
A 'final draft' is the version whose claims, counts, and URLs are frozen because the repository snapshot and manuscript should be released together without drift.
The '80-plus systems' count includes all tracked implementations in the maintained inventory, including borderline or lightly documented open-source projects that are still listed in the resources.
A 'reproducibility package' should be something an external reader can run to rebuild key tables and inspect the inclusion pipeline with minimal manual intervention.
A Friday deadline for deliverables tied to the repo means before midnight UTC because collaborators and users will pull from the tagged release globally.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to 'update the repo'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will 'update the repo' before the internal review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lina means refreshing the visible survey resources: taxonomy figure files, the curated comparison table, bibliographic links, and the README summary aligned with the manuscript.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun means delivering a fuller repository refresh: machine-readable inventory JSON/CSV, regeneration scripts, schema notes, cleaned metadata fields, and the public-facing docs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML paper workflows, 'update the repo' commonly sounds like a routine housekeeping task, so both treat the details as obvious extensions of normal release work rather than something needing explicit boundary-setting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to keeping the '80-plus systems' list current.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lina believes this means maintaining the set of systems that satisfy the survey's inclusion threshold for the main comparative catalog and appear in the manuscript tables.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun believes this means maintaining the broader tracked inventory in the repository, including provisional, lightly documented, or merged projects that still matter for completeness.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both want the survey to be comprehensive, the phrase '80-plus systems' feels like a stable factual reference even though they apply different inclusion standards beneath it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to prepare a 'reproducibility package' alongside the draft.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lina expects an internal audit bundle: the source spreadsheet, note columns for taxonomy decisions, citation-to-table traceability, and enough figure code to verify manuscript consistency.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun expects an external-facing artifact: a runnable pipeline that rebuilds key tables from the inventory, validates links, and outputs the release snapshot with minimal manual edits.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term 'reproducibility package' is standard and positively valenced in research settings, so each assumes the other shares their default procedural norm without probing the operational details.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the materials will be ready 'by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lina means by Friday evening in Pacific time so she can read the package before the weekend.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Arjun means by 23:59 UTC Friday as the timestamp for the tagged repo release.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Short internal planning meetings often use weekday deadlines conversationally, and both assume a shared norm without noticing that one is anchored to review timing while the other is anchored to release infrastructure.

turns.inner_thought: We need a crisp endgame. I do not want another late-stage debate about section order or catalog scope once senior coauthors see this. For me, the priority is making the manuscript look complete: taxonomy section polished, the comparative catalog stable, and the 80-plus systems count consistent with the systems that actually meet our inclusion bar in the paper tables. If those pieces are aligned, I can circulate confidently even if there is still some backend cleanup left in the repo.

By final draft, I mean polished prose, frozen section ordering, complete tables, and the resource links in place. The repo can still have minor cleanup afterward, as long as the manuscript-facing pieces are synchronized.
